key_insight: LSPO fixes a zero-gradient failure mode in RLVR by temporarily adding a low-rank LoRA scaffold to regenerate learning signal on "cliff" prompts where GRPO would otherwise get none.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical training-time patch for improving mathematical reasoning models without changing the final deployment model, since the adapter is used only during sampling and discarded afterward.
method: Detect prompts where all group rollouts fail and the RL advantage collapses to zero.
Fit a small LoRA adapter on ground-truth solutions for those cliff prompts.
Re-roll with base+adapter, importance-correct the successful samples, and update the base model with GRPO.
evidence_signal: On DeepMath-103K with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, LSPO matched or beat a DAPO baseline on all 16 benchmark/pass@k cells across 5 paired seeds, with an average +3.8-point gain and up to +10.7 on AIME24/pass@4.
watch_item: The extra supervised scaffold step and importance-sampling splice add training complexity and may be sensitive to how cliff prompts are detected, how the adapter is fit, and whether the correction remains stable.
paper_title: LoRA Scaffolded Policy Optimization (LSPO): A Sampling-Time Low-Rank Scaffold for Recovering Reinforcement-Learning Gradient on Zero-Reward Cliff Prompts
